title: Relative Homology Excision and Mayer Vietoris

items.title: Relative singular chain complex of a pair
The singular boundary descends to relative chains
items.strategy: Use that the inclusion A into X carries each singular chain of A to a chain of X and commutes with the boundary; the quotient differential is therefore well defined and still squares to zero.

items.title: Relative singular homology
Relative homology is functorial for maps of pairs
items.strategy: For a continuous f with f(A) contained in B, use the induced singular chain map to pass to quotient complexes, then pass to homology and check identities and composition on representatives.

items.title: Relative homology of the empty and total subspace
items.strategy: Identify the two quotient complexes C_*(X)/0 and C_*(X)/C_*(X) before taking homology, including every degree and the zero complex.

items.title: Long exact sequence of a pair in singular homology
items.strategy: Establish the short exact sequence C_*(A;G) to C_*(X;G) to C_*(X,A;G), invoke the established homological-algebra long exact sequence, and identify its maps with inclusion, quotient, and the relative connector.

items.title: Relative homology connecting homomorphism on cycles
The relative connecting map is independent of lift and representative
items.strategy: Compare two lifts and then two relative-cycle representatives. Their differences lie in the appropriate subcomplex or are relative boundaries, so their boundaries determine the same class in H_(n-1)(A;G).

items.title: Naturality of the long exact sequence of a pair
items.strategy: A map of pairs produces a morphism between the short exact quotient-complex sequences. Apply naturality of the homology connecting morphism and identify the other three maps on singular-chain representatives.

items.title: Barycenter and affine cone on a singular chain
Barycentric subdivision chain operator
Barycentric subdivision is a chain map
items.strategy: Induct on simplex dimension using the affine-cone boundary formula; pair the cone faces with the recursively subdivided faces to obtain S partial equals partial S.

items.title: Barycentric subdivision prism homotopy
Barycentric subdivision is chain homotopic to the identity
items.strategy: Use the recursively defined prism operator and its cone-boundary cancellations to prove S minus identity equals partial T plus T partial in every degree, including degree zero.

items.title: Mesh of iterated barycentric subdivision tends to zero
items.strategy: Prove the dimension-n mesh factor n/(n+1) for one barycentric subdivision, then iterate that strict contraction; treat dimension zero separately rather than dividing by zero.

items.title: Cover-small singular chain subcomplex
Every finite singular chain becomes cover-small after enough subdivision
items.strategy: Pull the open cover back along each singular simplex, use compactness and a Lebesgue number on its standard simplex, apply mesh decay, then take the finite maximum of the resulting least depths over the chain support only.

items.title: Cover-small singular chains compute singular homology
items.strategy: Use enough subdivision and S minus identity equals partial T plus T partial to prove surjectivity on cycles and injectivity on boundaries separately for the inclusion of the cover-small subcomplex.

items.title: Cover-small inclusion is a chain homotopy equivalence
items.strategy: On each singular-simplex generator use its least compatible subdivision depth, build the compatible finite-depth comparison and homotopy recursively, and extend linearly; this strengthens the homology-isomorphism result without claiming one global subdivision depth.

items.title: Excision for singular homology
items.strategy: For closure(Z) contained in interior(A), compare relative chains with the cover-small quotient for the cover X minus closure(Z), interior(A). The small-chain equivalence identifies this quotient with C_*(X minus Z,A minus Z) and C_*(X,A).

items.title: Good pair for singular homology
Homology of a good pair is reduced homology of the quotient
items.strategy: Excise the complement of a deformation-retracting neighbourhood and compare the pair long exact sequence with the reduced sequence of the quotient, checking the degree-zero and nonempty-A conventions explicitly.

items.title: Two-open-cover small chains are the sum of the two singular subcomplexes
items.strategy: A generator subordinate to the two-member cover lies entirely in U or entirely in V, giving the sum; conversely each summand is cover-small. Keep the intersection statement at the chain level separate for the next short exact sequence.

items.title: Short exact two-open singular-chain Mayer--Vietoris sequence
items.strategy: Use c maps to (c,-c) and (a,b) maps to a+b. The chain-level intersection C_*(U) intersection C_*(V)=C_*(U intersection V) and the preceding sum lemma prove exactness degreewise and preserve the chosen signs.

items.title: Mayer--Vietoris sequence in singular homology
items.strategy: Apply the homology long exact sequence to the signed short exact sequence and use cover-small homology equivalence to replace its final complex by C_*(X;G), identifying every map and connector.

items.title: Mayer--Vietoris connecting class
The Mayer--Vietoris connector is independent of small-chain decomposition
items.strategy: Subtract two cover-small decompositions of the same subdivided cycle. Exactness of the signed chain sequence expresses their difference through the overlap, and its boundary calculation shows the two overlap classes agree.

items.title: Naturality of singular Mayer--Vietoris
items.strategy: A cover-preserving map gives a morphism of signed short exact chain sequences. Apply connecting-map naturality and the natural cover-small comparison, then identify the explicit connecting classes.

items.title: Simplicial and singular homology agree for simplicial complexes
items.strategy: Use the established simplicial-to-singular chain map. Reduce a finite cycle to a finite subcomplex, prove the local simplex comparison, and induct over its skeleta before passing back to the full complex.

items.title: Homology of spheres
items.strategy: Cover S^n by two contractible open hemispherical neighbourhoods with intersection homotopy equivalent to S^(n-1), use Mayer--Vietoris inductively, and isolate S^0 and reduced degree zero as base cases.

items.title: Well-pointed based space
Suspension isomorphism in reduced singular homology
items.strategy: Use the two contractible cone neighbourhoods of the suspension and their intersection deformation retracting to X. Mayer--Vietoris gives the degree shift, with the library's explicit empty-space suspension convention kept outside the well-pointed hypothesis.

title: Relative Homology Excision and Mayer Vietoris — Examples

items.title: Relative homology of a disk and its boundary
items.strategy: Apply the pair long exact sequence to (D^n,S^(n-1)), using contractibility of the disk and the sphere calculation; print the n=0 convention separately.

items.title: Relative homology of an interval and its endpoints
items.strategy: Write the low-degree pair sequence for (I,partial I), use the two components of the endpoints, and identify the connecting map on an oriented interval chain.

items.title: First barycentric subdivision of a triangle
items.strategy: List the six oriented small triangles ordered by barycentres of nested faces, then cancel their interior edges to verify the boundary formula in dimension two.

items.title: Cover-small chains for the two-arc cover of a circle
items.strategy: Choose two proper open arcs covering the circle, subdivide an explicit loop until each edge is subordinate, and compute the overlap boundary class that is the Mayer--Vietoris connector.

items.title: Mayer--Vietoris computation of sphere homology
items.strategy: Use slightly enlarged open hemispheres, identify their intersection with S^(n-1), and follow the exact sequence through the inductive degree calculation rather than merely citing the sphere corollary.

items.title: Mayer--Vietoris computation of the torus first homology
items.strategy: Use a two-cylinder open cover of T^2 whose intersection has two annular components. Identify the maps on H_0 and H_1, then use exactness to obtain H_1(T^2;G) and expose the two generator classes.

items.title: Excision can fail without closure inside interior
items.strategy: Take X=[0,1], A=[0,1/2], and Z={1/2}. Compute both relative H_0 groups directly from components to show that deleting the boundary point changes the group.

items.title: One subdivision depth does not make all singular simplices cover-small
items.strategy: For a fixed two-arc cover of the circle, give singular loops with increasing oscillation. Each finite chain has a depth, but no one depth handles the whole singular-simplex basis.

items.title: Relative homology is not the homology of the set difference
items.strategy: Compare (D^n,S^(n-1)) with D^n minus S^(n-1). The pair has its nonzero relative group in degree n, whereas the open ball is contractible, so quotient chains cannot be replaced by complement chains.
